array-basics.summary: Arrays are fundamental data structures that store elements in contiguous memory locations, allowing O(1) access time through indexing. They are fixed-size and provide efficient element retrieval.
array-basics.whyItMatters: Arrays are the foundation for more complex data structures and are used extensively in algorithms. Understanding array operations is crucial for writing efficient code and solving computational problems.
commonMisconceptions: Arrays are always the best choice for storing data
Insertion and deletion are as fast as access
Arrays can grow dynamically in all languages

linked-list.summary: Linked lists are dynamic data structures where each element (node) contains data and a reference to the next node. They excel at insertions and deletions but have slower access times than arrays.
linked-list.whyItMatters: Linked lists demonstrate the trade-offs in data structure design between access speed and modification flexibility. They're fundamental to understanding pointers and memory management.
commonMisconceptions: Linked lists are always better than arrays
Accessing middle elements is still O(1)
All linked lists are doubly linked
